mainEntity.name: How much does YouTube pay for 1,000 views?

acceptedAnswer.text: YouTube pays creators between $1.50 and $25.00+ per 1,000 views based on RPM. Entertainment and gaming channels earn $1.50 to $4.00 RPM, while high-CPM niches like Personal Finance, SaaS, and Tech generate $12.00 to $32.00 RPM after YouTube's 45% revenue cut.

mainEntity.name: How much does YouTube pay for 100,000 views?

acceptedAnswer.text: For 100,000 views, YouTube pays approximately $200 to $2,800. General entertainment channels in Tier 1 countries net $250 to $500, tech channels earn $800 to $1,500, and finance or business software channels earn $1,800 to $2,800+.

mainEntity.name: How much does YouTube pay for 1 million views?

acceptedAnswer.text: 1 million views generates between $2,000 and $25,000 in AdSense revenue. In general lifestyle and entertainment, 1M views nets $2,500 to $4,500. In high-value educational or software niches, 1M views produces $15,000 to $30,000 in AdSense plus $10,000+ in sponsorships.

mainEntity.name: What percentage does YouTube take from creators?

acceptedAnswer.text: On standard long-form videos, YouTube retains 45% of total gross advertising revenue, paying the creator 55%. On YouTube Shorts, YouTube allocates 45% of the shared Creator Pool revenue to creators and retains 55%.

mainEntity.name: At what income should a YouTuber form an S-Corporation?

acceptedAnswer.text: The standard financial threshold to elect S-Corp tax status is $60,000 to $80,000 in annual net creator profit. Below $60K, additional payroll processing and corporate tax filing costs ($1,200-$2,500/yr) offset tax benefits.

mainEntity.name: How does an S-Corp save YouTubers money on taxes?

acceptedAnswer.text: In a single-member LLC, 100% of creator net profit is hit by the 15.3% FICA self-employment tax. With an S-Corp election, only the W-2 reasonable salary pays FICA, while the remaining distribution flows through completely free of the 15.3% payroll tax.

mainEntity.name: What business expenses can YouTubers write off?

acceptedAnswer.text: YouTubers can write off cameras, lenses, lighting, microphones, editing computers, software subscriptions, contractor fees for editors, home office square footage, internet, and travel directly related to video shoots.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between CPM and RPM on YouTube?
